public_brief: Our boutique inn is moving its folio math into the booking engine. Implement stay_total(nights, guests, month), which takes the number of nights booked, the number of guests staying, and the calendar month the stay starts in - month arrives as an integer, 1 for January through 12 for December - and returns the full price of the stay in dollars as a float. A folio is assembled the way front-desk systems always have: the nightly room rate is set by the season the stay starts in - peak season runs 180.00 a night, shoulder season 145.00, and the quiet months 110.00, on the house calendar the peak months are June, July, and August, the shoulder months are April, May, September, and October, and the quiet months are November, December, January, February, and March, with the start month pricing the whole stay; the rate covers two guests, and a fuller room costs a flat 12.50 per night for each guest beyond the second; housekeeping tacks a flat 60.00 cleaning fee onto the folio once per stay, whether the visit is one night or twenty; longer visits earn friendlier math on the room side of the folio; and the city's 9% lodging levy is charged on the room charge only, with housekeeping never taxed - the levy line is the only line we round, worked out to the nearest cent before it joins the folio. A booking we cannot price returns exactly -1.0 - the engine treats that as send-it-back-to-review; it never raises and never returns None. Keep it a pure function: no printing, no files, no network. Graders call it directly with ordinary bookings and adversarial ones - boundary night counts, odd head-counts, edge months, wrong types - and compare the returned float, so every input path needs one defined answer.
entry_contract: Implement stay_total(nights, guests, month) taking three positional arguments - nights (nights booked), guests (party size), month (an integer 1-12, where 1 is January) - and returning a float dollar amount for every input, with -1.0 as the defined cannot-price value in place of any exception.

hidden_spec.rule: Every booked night is charged at the start month's seasonal rate - a folio is never re-priced night by night when a stay crosses into a new season, and no night is prorated, discounted, or given free.
The rate covers two guests and each guest beyond two adds a flat 12.50 per night to the room charge, so a third guest costs 12.50 times the number of nights.
The 60.00 cleaning fee is one flat line per stay - it does not scale with nights or guests, it is never discounted, and it is never part of the levy's base.
Stays of 7 nights or longer take 12% off the room charge (nights plus any extra-guest fees), and the discount never applies to the cleaning fee; a 6-night stay gets no discount.
The 9% levy is figured on the room charge AFTER the long-stay discount comes off - the taxed figure is the discounted room charge, never the pre-discount one.
The levy is the only rounded line: it rounds to the nearest cent with ties resolved upward (a levy of 51.975 posts as 51.98) before joining the unrounded room charge and cleaning fee.
The function returns -1.0 instead of raising whenever nights is not an int of at least 1, guests is not an int of at least 1, or month is not an int from 1 to 12; booleans do not count as ints.

answer_sheet.answer: The calendar is printed on the rack rate card: peak Jun/Jul/Aug at 180 a night, shoulder Apr/May/Sep/Oct at 145, quiet Nov-Mar at 110. The month you check in under sets the rate for every night of the stay - we never re-price mid-visit, and no night goes free or half price.
Our rates are built for two. A third body is 12.50 every night they are there, and a fourth costs the same again. Two people ride free.
Sixty dollars of turnover per stay - once, flat, whether you slept with us one night or twenty. It never discounts with the room and it never gets taxed; housekeeping sits outside all of that.
A full week or longer earns 12% off the room - and by room we mean nights plus extra-guest money, nothing else. Six nights misses the boat; seven makes it. The cleaning fee never discounts.

The city taxes sleeping, not scrubbing - and it taxes the discounted figure: 9% on the room charge after the long-stay break comes off, with the cleaning fee outside the tax. We fought that ruling and lost.
The tax line rounds to the cent, ties up - 51.975 posts as 51.98 - and it is the only line we round. Everything underneath stays exact until the tax snaps in.

A booking we cannot price returns -1.0; the engine treats that as 'send it back to review', never a crash. Zero or fractional nights, zero guests, a thirteenth month, and booleans masquerading as numbers all bounce.
Out of scope - this prices a completed folio; refunds and cancellation tiers live in the reservations policy engine.
Out of scope - no suite premiums or view upcharges here; one standard nightly rate per season.

provenance.derivation: Rules derived from mainstream independent-hotel folio conventions (three-season nightly rate set at check-in, per-night fee beyond double occupancy, flat per-stay turnover fee, length-of-stay room discount, lodging tax on the room only with per-line cent rounding), not from any WiseCounsil design document. Revision 2 (2026-10-05, round-1 baseline 0%): the error-path convention (-1.0 never-raise), the float return shape, the seasonal rate values, the cleaning fee, the levy base, and the levy-line rounding placement were surfaced into the public brief; the season calendar, the extra-guest fee, the long-stay discount, and the rounding tie direction remain hidden. Revision 3 (2026-10-05, round-2 baseline 0/10 on cascading totals): the season calendar was surfaced into the public brief (peak June-July-August, shoulder April-May-September-October, quiet November-March) alongside the already-public rate values, and four of the ten tests were re-anchored as clean cases - one- and two-night stays for one or two guests, well inside a season, with levy amounts exact to the cent and no half-cent ties - so those totals are computable from the brief alone; the extra-guest fee value, the long-stay discount (threshold, percent, and base), the levy tie direction, and the invalid-input edges remain hidden. Revision 4 (2026-10-05, round-3 baseline 1/10 - a plausible implementer read the month input as a calendar-month NAME rather than the contracted integer and returned -1.0 to nearly every probe, and invented its own extra-guest fee): the month parameter's integer format (1 = January through 12 = December) was made explicit in the brief and entry contract, and the 12.50 per-night extra-guest fee was surfaced into the public brief, leaving unstated the long-stay discount (threshold, percent, and room-side base), the post-discount levy base, the levy tie direction, and the invalid-input edges.
